title: norite voice --json
description:
The machine-readable output of `norite voice status`, `join` and `leave` (M28), and since M34 `mute`, `unmute`, `deafen`, `undeafen`, `local-mute`, `local-unmute`, `streams` and `processing`, and since M35 `mode`: how the daemon's voice call stands after the command.

Versioned source of truth (CLAUDE.md rule 15): a change to what these commands print ships with a change to this file in the same commit. Every field is always present.

`join` prints the status once the call is up; a join refused or failed prints nothing on stdout and exits 4 or 1 with the reason. `leave` prints the status after the call has ended, its worker gone.

state.description: idle: no call. joining: a join under way, which another client may have asked for. in_call: connected to the voice server, which has said ready.

channel.description: The call's channel id while there is a call, or empty.

reason.description: Why the last call ended, or why the last join failed, for a person; `left` when it was left; empty when nothing has ended yet.

ended_in_call.description: Whether `reason` is why a call that was up ended (true), or why a join failed before it was (false). False while there is a call, and before any (M33).

available.description: Whether this daemon can join a call at all: since M33 any daemon signed in, over its connection to the instance.

unavailable.description: Why not, when `available` is false. Empty otherwise.

processing.description: The call's audio processing as its join asked, from config.toml's voice keys (M30), while there is a call; null when there is none.

microphone.description: What the call's microphone is doing (M32), as the voice worker last said; null before it has said. Kept after a call its devices ended, both failing as it started, so its end can be explained; null after any other end, after `leave` and at the next join. `join` prints once the call is up and this is past `opening`, or after 3 s.

speakers.description: What the call's speakers are doing (M32), as for `microphone`.

rights.description: What the account may do in the call (M33), as its instance last said; null while no call has been answered. `send` is false under a moderator's server mute or in a channel where the account lacks SPEAK, `hear` false under a server deafen. This client applies them, and the text output says so.

self.description: What you set on yourself (M34), in a call or not, which holds until you sign out and which everybody in the channel sees. A deafen mutes too.

local_mutes.description: Whom you muted for yourself alone (M34), sorted, as user ids: the voice server sends you nothing of them. Never a report. [] for nobody.

max_streams.description: How many people you hear at once (M34), 1 to 3, or null for everybody the call has room for.

speaking.description: Who the voice server says is speaking now (M34), as user ids, those you muted for yourself included; [] with no call.

dsp.description: What the call's audio processing is doing (M34), where processing is what was asked: null with no call and before the voice worker has said.

reason.description: Why it failed, the voice worker's words, with what a terminal would act on escaped; empty otherwise.

input.description: How the call's microphone is let through (M35), while there is a call; null when there is none.

mode.description: voice: what the noise suppressor takes for a voice is sent. push_to_talk: what is said while the key is down.

key.description: The push-to-talk key as asked, as in ctrl+shift+space.

hotkey.description: Empty by voice. By push-to-talk: being registered, waiting for the desktop to ask the person about it, registered, or unavailable, reason saying why, when nothing is sent.

reason.description: Why the key is unavailable, the OS's or the desktop's words, with what a terminal would act on escaped; and, registered, what to do where the desktop binds the key in its own settings and named none; empty otherwise.

trigger.description: The key as the desktop says it is bound, which on Linux's portal the person chooses, escaped as reason is; empty where the OS takes the key as asked.

held.description: Whether the key is down now.

state.description: opening: being opened, or opened and not yet delivering. open: delivering audio. asking: macOS is asking whether norite-daemon may use the microphone. refused: the OS or the person refused it; the text output names the setting that changes it. no_device: there is none to use. no_session: the account is not logged in at the machine, whoever else is, so nothing it runs may use a device (Linux). failed: anything else, `reason` saying what.

reason.description: The voice worker's words on what went wrong, or empty.
